items.summary: TSMC reported consolidated revenue of about NT$511.86 billion (approx. US$16.1 billion) for September 2026. That was up 54.6% from NT$330.98 billion a year earlier and down 0.6% from August, the company said on October 8.

items.title: Hanmi wins rare Samsung order amid US$5 billion chip substrate expansion
items.summary: South Korea's Hanmi Semiconductor has secured a KRW24.48 billion (approx. US$18.3 million) equipment order from Samsung Electro-Mechanics, a rare deal with a Samsung Group affiliate after years of limited business following a patent dispute. The contract comes a week after Samsung Electro-Mechanics announced a KRW6.78 trillion expansion of its AI server substrate business, as demand for advanced chip packaging continues to grow.

items.title: Samsung to exit in-house automotive AP, focus on high-margin chips
items.summary: Samsung Electronics' System LSI division is reportedly planning a retreat from the automotive application processor (AP) business and launching a major restructuring, with a future focus on high-margin areas such as image sensors and mobile system-on-chip (SoC) products. Analysts say Samsung is seeking to improve profitability in its non-memory businesses through a selection and concentration strategy after years of losses at System LSI and its foundry operations.

items.title: Microsoft readies Windows for AI agents as third-party agents such as Meta's Muse spread
items.summary: Beyond Surface hardware, Microsoft used its October 7 event to change how Windows runs, routes, and contains AI agents, as third-party agents such as Meta's Muse draw privacy complaints and, according to a Bank of America analyst, threaten platform owners' control of transactions. Apple and Google have expanded agent tools in their operating systems this year, and Reuters described Microsoft's push as a challenge to Apple's effort to bring more AI into personal devices.

items.title: Marvell's custom AI chip upgrade points to a broader fight over peripherals
items.summary: Marvell's higher long-term target for custom AI chip revenue suggests the market for artificial intelligence hardware is widening beyond accelerators, into management chips, storage, memory, and networking. The shift could benefit Taiwanese design firms, but it also raises the bar for custom silicon expertise and customer access.

items.title: Nvidia's RTX Spark gives Windows on Arm its strongest shot yet at x86's high end
items.summary: Nvidia's entry into the Windows PC market with its Arm-based RTX Spark platform is giving Microsoft's Windows on Arm strategy a new test: whether Arm can move beyond being a niche alternative and meaningfully challenge the long-standing dominance of x86.

items.summary: As soaring memory prices are forecast to cut PC shipments, a new class of expensive machines built to run large AI models locally, from Nvidia's RTX Spark laptops to Apple's Mac Studio and AMD's Ryzen AI Max systems, is arriving at the top of the market, where Gartner says higher memory costs could sharpen the focus on premium devices. items.summary: Before generative AI rose and Nvidia GPUs came to dominate the market, the central processing unit (CPU) was the main compute engine for servers. items.title: Samsung Electronics posts record quarterly profit in preliminary results
items.summary: Samsung Electronics has become the first South Korean company to clear KRW100 trillion in operating profit in a single quarter, a milestone that shows how heavily the company now leans on a memory market where, by analysts' reckoning, suppliers hold pricing power. The open questions are whether high-bandwidth memory (HBM) contracts can extend that run into 2027, and how long the company's consumer-device arm can absorb the rising component costs that the same boom creates.
